text:
Samir: morning team :wave: I'm taking primary for the 06:00-14:00 window. Secondary is @Mei. Quick heads-up: I saw a small spike in 5xxs on payment routing last night around 02:40. No active pager right now but worth a preflight check.
Mei: thanks — I'll shadow for the first 30. passing on token-level costs alert to infra. anything I should prewarm? :eyes:
Samir: prewarm kv-cache shards for us-east-1 and eu-west-1. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-stall (quick checks section). Also confirm autoscale status for the dedicated pool `ded-cc-1`.
Mei: got it. I'll run the preflight checklist and report back.
incident-bot: Pager suppressed: payment-reroute-5xx (severity: P2) — last seen 02:42 UTC. If errors > 0.5% for 15m, escalate.
Jordan: I'm on call for escalations if it spikes. Quick note: if response latencies > 2s on reroute service, fallback to model-variant b-quant.
Samir: adding the two most-used runbook snippets here for fast copy:
```
# Check KV cache health
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://kv-proxy.us-east-1.internal/health | jq .cache_status
# Restart shard if status == degraded
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/kv-shard-3
```
Mei: preflight results: kv cache status shows `healthy`, shard 3 replicaset at 3/3, autoscale target for `ded-cc-1` is 75% CPU (policy OK). No active deploys.
Priya: FYI I left a note on the routing team's ticket — they throttled a partner's webhook last night which probably caused the 5xx burst. Ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/RT-4321
Samir: good catch. Action items: 1) Mei to keep primary monitoring dashboards open 2) Jordan standby for rollback 3) Priya to liaise with routing. If anything spikes, tag `@oncall-escalate`.
Luis: quick pointer — if KV cache miss rate climbs, enable prefix caching per runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefix-cache. Command: `redis-cli -h kv-proxy config set prefix_caching on` (only for warm periods).
Mei: watchlist updated. I'm also enabling alert noise suppression on infra metrics for minor blips (2m window).
Samir: reminder for handoff at 13:30: leave short note about any open mitigation and whether we've applied any temporary config changes. Use template below in handoff channel:
```
Handoff: primary->secondary
Window: 06:00-14:00
Primary: Samir
Secondary: Mei
Open items:
- routing ticket RT-4321 (Priya)
- kv-cache prewarm completed (yes)
- autoscale policy unchanged
Mitigations applied: none
Expected next checks: 10:00, 12:00
```
Jordan: if we get a P1, escalate to mobile-sre and ping the exec channel after 15 mins.
incident-bot: Reminder scheduled in 1h: do the 10:00 checkpoint.
Priya: will follow up with routing team and post any partner-side fixes here.
Mei: quick Q — if we need to roll back reroute, what's the single-line rollback command?
Samir: `kubectl -n routing rollout undo deploy/reroute-service --to-revision=3` — documented in runbook. Also we have a canary toggle: `curl -X POST https://feature-toggle.internal/toggles/reroute-canary -d '{"on":false}'`
Luis: added runbook shortlink to pinned messages for the shift.
Samir: thanks. I'll ping again at 09:50 for the warm handoff checklist. Keep notes minimal and action-oriented. :thumbsup:
Mei: acknowledged. logging check-ins to the handoff doc: https://redwood.internal/handovers/shift-1749991234
Jordan: quick reminder to update incident status if you escalate — small updates reduce noisy pings.
Samir: closing primary prep. If anyone sees >0.5% errors or latency >2s for 10m, call the bridge and tag `@oncall-escalate`.
ops-runbooks-bot: Runbook links for this thread: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-preflight, https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-stall, https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefix-cache
Mei: copy. standing by.
